editorial:
Imagine landing in San Francisco with nothing but a dream and a laugh that makes everyone around you start giggling too. You get to meet a lonely Egyptian man trying to survive in America while his home country is falling apart during the Arab Spring. He is a sweet guy, but he has the worst luck you have ever seen. To make things worse, the only person who can help him get his legal papers is a lawyer who cares more about money than people. It is a wild ride that mixes sad moments with some really funny situations, making you root for the underdog from the very first scene.

The acting is top-notch because the lead actor makes you feel his stress and his joy without saying much. The pacing is quick, though some of the legal talk can be a bit slow. You will love how the movie handles the struggle of being an outsider. It is a great pick for a Friday night when you want something with a heart.
endingExplained: In the end, the greedy lawyer tries to scam the main character one last time, but his plan backfires. The main character's contagious laugh actually wins over a government official who was supposed to deport him. Because of a lucky break and some unexpected kindness, he finally gets his residency papers. He ends the movie no longer alone, having found a small community of friends who love him for who he is.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about underdogs and fish-out-of-water comedies.
